SPECIFICATION FOR CYLINDER LIN£RS 
FOR INTERNAL COMBUSTION ENGINES 

( First Revision ) 



1. Scope— Specif iesteciinical supply conditions for cast iron cylinder liners, dry and wet types 
applicable to reciprocating internal combustion engines working on 2-8troke or 4-stroke cycles. 

n 

1 .1 Wet cylinder liner supplied with outside surface as cast are also covered. 

2. Definitions 

2.1 Dry Cy Under LiMr — fi^ cyliner liner which does not experience any direct contact with the 
ergine cooling media. This type of liner Is in contact with the cylinder block material over its entire 
length or nearly its entire length. 

2.1.1 Dry liners may be of flanged type (sea Fig. 1A) or without flange {see Fig. IB).

3. Material — Cylinder liners shall be manufactured from good quality close-grained cast iron. 
The castings shall be produced either by centrifugal casting or by gravity die casting in metal 
or sand moulds or a combination of the two. The material of the cylinder liner shall satisfy 3.1 
and 3.2 read with its subclauses.

face of the liner in the cast condition, in the middle third of the cross-section thickness, according 
to IS : 1789-1961 'Method for Brinell hardness test for grey cast iron' and shall conform to the 
following:

Metallic mould castings

such liners Is 45 to 50 HRC. 



3.2 Micro-structure 

3.2.1 Graphite — T\\Q graphite shall be fine to medium lamellar and ehaU be uniformaUy 
distributed. For centrifugal castings in metallic moulds, nest formations of graphite and inter- 
dendritic segregations randomly oriented are only permitted to the extant that they are unavoidable 
and as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. Oriented and inter-dendritic graphite 
shall not be present in sand castings. 

3.2.2 MatrAr— The matrix shall have a pearlitic-sorbitlc structure without the presence of 
cementite. A maximum of 5 percent ferrite is permissible.

3.2.4 Sl/vsf^/i/MW/i^ — Stress-relieving in the rough machined condition shall be as agreed to 
between the purchassr and the manufacturer.

specified in Table 2.

5. Surface Finish — The surface finish on the finish machined liner shall be in accordance with 
Table 3.

Roughness values lesser than the limits specified in Table 3 shall be mutually agreed to 
between the purchaser and the manufacturer. The bore surface of the liners shall be finished by 
honing with a cross-hatch pattern having an included angle between 30^ and 60'' in the horizontal 
plane. 

6. Inspection 

6.1 Bange of Inspection — Shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 

6.2 Dimensional Inspection — AW dmenslons shaW be checked against values given on the finished 
part drawings in conjunction with permissible tolerances according to Table 2. 

6.2.1 Grading for selective assembly ^ When assembly requirement calls for closer fit tolerance 
than obtainable with the standard, grading of outer diameter and/or inner diameter of the liner may 
be resorted to as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 

6.3 Boughness Inspection — \X shall be carried out in accordance with IS : 3073-1967 'Assessment 
of surface roughness' on the bore surface in the region over which the piston rings operate. 

6.3.1 The roughness on the outer seating surface may be estimated visually or by comparative 
checking. 

6.4 Micro-structure Bxamination 

6.4.1 The sample for micro-structure examination shall be taken from the bore running surface 
at a place in the region over which the piston rings would operate. 



IS : 6750 . 1986 

6.4.2 The following scales of inegnification shall bo used for determining the micro -structure: 

Graphite 100 x 

Matrix 500 x 

Phosphide eutectic 1 x or 1 00 x 

For estimating the permissible ferrite content the average over a surface area of approximately 
1 mm* shall be taken. 

B3 Hardness-- The Brinell hardness shall be measured on the machined upper end face of the 
liner as specified in IS : 1500-1983 'Method for Brinell hardness test forWtaliic materials {second 
revision)'. An fiverage value of three readings unlformally distributed over the circumference on 
the upper end face of the liner shall be taken as the actual hardness value. 

Not« — The distence of the centra of the impresiion shall bo at loost twice the ball diomotcr from the edge of the 
lir>er. 

7. Acceptonca 

7.1 All characteristics in accordance with this standard shall be chekced at the final inspection by 
the manufacturer. 

7.2 Minor casting defects will be acceptable provided these do not have any influence on the life 
or performance of the liners. A guideline regarding such permissible casting defects is given in 
Appendix A. 

8. Marking 

8.1 Minimum markings on the outer surface of the cylinder liner shall be as follows*. 

a) Name« trade name or registered trade-mark of the manufacturer; 

b) Application; and 

c) Size. 

Any additional markings shall be decided between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 

8.2 iSf Certification i\4arking—' Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8.3 The marking shall preferably be done with a suitable etching media which shall not get easily 
eroded. 

9. Packing 

9.1 Liners shall be adequately protected with anti- corrosive protective media and suitably 
wrapped. 

9.2 Each liner shall be placed in a well-fitting carton and further suitably created to avoid damage 
during transport. 

9.3 In case of overseas transport, additional specifications available tor such transport shall be 
followed. 

10. Surface Coatings — Surface of wet liners in contact with water may be coated with suitable 
anti-cavitation surface coatings as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer.

APPENDIX A 

{CiausB 7,2) 

ACCEPTANCE STANDARD FOR CASTING DEFECTS AND 
DAMAGES ON CYLINDER LINERS 

A-1 . Casting Defects 

A-1.1 Acceptability of casting defects Is to be decided in accordance with location, size and nature 
of defect. 

A-1 -2 For determining the location, the machined cylinder liner bore shall be divided into 3 zones 
which are to be indicated on the drawing by the purchaser as follows: 

Zone A » Above the piston ring path 

Zone B *« Piston ring path 

Zone C » Below the piston ring path 

A-1 .3 Defects in Cy finder Liner Bore — Uniformaliy distributed defects, such as blow holes and 
microporosity are permissible in the finish machined cylinder liner bore in accordance with the 
following table: 

Number of Defects for Bore Die 

Zone Maximum / * ^ 

Die of Defects Up to 50 mm Above 50 Up to Above 1 50 mm 

mm 150 mm 

A 1 2 3 5 

B Nil Nil Nil Nil 

C 2 3 5 5 

A-1 .3.1 For a distance of 6 mm from either end of the cylinder, no casting defects are 
permissible. 

A-1 .3.2 The depth of the defect shall be not more than 20 percent of the wall thickness subject 
to a maximum of 1 mm. 

A-1 .3.3 The distance of the defect-spots from one another shall be not less than 50 mm. 

A-1 .4 Defects on the Outer Surface of Cylinder Liner 

A-1 .4.1 No defects are permissible on sealing faces of the outer surfaces. 

A-1 .4.2 On the faces of the outer surafce where no sealing takes place, uniformaliy distributed 
defects according to the following table are permissible. 

Zone Meximum Die of Defects for Number of Defects for 

Wet Liner Dry Liner 

A 1 3 4 5 

B 3 3 5 6

A-1 ,4.3 With regard to distance of defects from one another and from the ends of the cylinder 
liners, those outlined in A-1 .3 are valid. Defects in the bore and on the outer surface shall not lie 
on one another.

A-2. Maohanical Surface DamagM— Mechanical damagea in tha procasa of machining ara 
parmitsibla ao long aa they do not affact tha parfonnanca of tha cylindar linara. 

A-2.1 Dafacta undar thia category ara: 

a ) Groovaa on watar iaclcat which ara cauaed by tha return motion of tha tools; 

b) Grooves on the seating surfaces, provided no material #i8S been removed and provided 
the seating surfaces are not simultaneously used for sealing; and 

c ) Small out-breaka in the region of the slotted portion for the connected rod. 

A*U Damages on the cylinder bore, aa also on the aealing aurfacea of the liner, are not 
permissible. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in the year 1972. The revision is being Issued in the light 
of experience gained In the implementation of the standard by the manufacturers and the users. 

In this revision following changes have been made: 

a ) Wet linera with the outside surface as cast are also being covered; 

b) Linera have been classified into two groups according to hardness, namely, 'soft' and 
'hard' to cover the requirements of high powered engines; 

c ) Measurement of hardness has been made more specific; 

d) Tolerancaa for chamfera according to IS : 2102-1969 have been included; 

a) Surface roughneaa for ground outer seating surface have been included; and 

f ) Grading of linera for selective assembly have been Included.
